summary: 太平洋岛民的祖先怎样跨海定居，不能仅凭早期航海传奇解释。研究者亲身航行、测量独木舟性能并借助其他实验和模型，重新认识传统航海技术。
logic: 比较实航与船只测量等研究
理解岛民技能及其传承

paragraphs.brief: 太平洋的许多小岛没有人类，直到大约2000年前，今天的岛民的祖先在远洋独木舟中从东南亚航行。
sentences: The many tiny islands of the Pacific Ocean had no human population until ancestors of today’s islanders sailed from Southeast Asia in ocean-going canoes approximately 2,000 years ago.
太平洋的许多小岛没有人类，直到大约2000年前，今天的岛民的祖先在远洋独木舟中从东南亚航行。
At the present time, the debate continues about exactly how they migrated such vast distances across the ocean, without any of the modern technologies we take for granted.
目前，关于它们如何在海洋中迁徙如此之远而没有我们认为理所当然的现代技术的辩论仍在继续。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然一些二十世纪早期英勇航海者船队的作家的浪漫远见被后来的调查人员认为是夸大了，但直到1956年美国历史学家安德鲁·夏普发表他的研究成果时，才开始对太平洋的破坏行为进行深思熟虑的评估。
sentences: Although the romantic vision of some early twentieth-century writers of fleets of heroic navigators simultaneously setting sail had come to be considered by later investigators to be exaggerated, no considered assessment of Pacific voyaging was forthcoming until 1956 when the American historian Andrew Sharp published his research.
虽然一些二十世纪早期英勇航海者船队的作家的浪漫远见被后来的调查人员认为是夸大了，但直到1956年美国历史学家安德鲁·夏普发表他的研究成果时，才开始对太平洋的破坏行为进行深思熟虑的评估。

Sharp challenged the ‘heroic vision’ by asserting that the expertise of the navigators was limited, and that the settlement of the islands was not systematic, being more dependent on good fortune by drifting canoes.
Sharp对 " 英雄观 " 提出质疑，声称航海者的专门知识有限，岛上的定居不是系统性的，因为漂流独木舟更依赖幸运。
Sharp’s theory was widely challenged, and deservedly so.
夏普的理论受到广泛质疑，理应受到质疑。
If nothing else, however, it did spark renewed interest in the topic and precipitated valuable new research.
然而，如果不这样做的话，它确实激发了人们对这个专题的兴趣，并激发了宝贵的新研究。

paragraphs.brief: 自1960年代以来，已经进行了大量的调查，大多数调查都属于 " 非武装主席 " 类别。
sentences: Since the 1960s a wealth of investigations has been conducted, and most of them, thankfully, have been of the ‘non-armchair’ variety.
自1960年代以来，已经进行了大量的调查，大多数调查都属于 " 非武装主席 " 类别。

While it would be wrong to denigrate all ‘armchair’ research — that based on an examination of available published materials — it has turned out that so little progress had been made in the area of Pacific voyaging because most writers relied on the same old sources — travelers’ journals or missionary narratives compiled by unskilled observers.
虽然贬低所有 " 武器主席 " 研究(根据对现有出版材料的审查)是错误的，但事实证明，太平洋的破坏活动进展甚微，因为大多数作者都依赖同样的老来源 -- -- 旅行者杂志或由非熟练观察员汇编的传教士叙事。
After Sharp, this began to change, and researchers conducted most of their investigations not in libraries, but in the field.
夏普之后，情况开始发生变化，研究人员不是在图书馆而是在实地进行调查。

paragraphs.brief: 1965年，大卫·刘易斯，一位医生，一位有经验的游艇员，开始使用他自己的独特哲学：他乘坐他多年来拥有的游艇，在群岛上航行，以便与那些仍然使用传统方法在海上寻找出路的人接触。
sentences: In 1965, David Lewis, a physician and experienced yachtsman, set to work using his own unique philosophy: he took the yacht he had owned for many years and navigated through the islands in order to contact those men who still find their way at sea using traditional methods.
1965年，大卫·刘易斯，一位医生，一位有经验的游艇员，开始使用他自己的独特哲学：他乘坐他多年来拥有的游艇，在群岛上航行，以便与那些仍然使用传统方法在海上寻找出路的人接触。

He then accompanied these men, in their traditional canoes, on test voyages from which all modern instruments were banished from sight, though Lewis secretly used them to confirm the navigator’s calculations.
他随后陪同这些人在传统的独木舟上试航，将所有现代仪器从视线中排除出去，尽管Lewis秘密利用它们证实航海者的计算。
His most famous such voyage was a return trip of around 1,000 nautical miles between two islands in mid-ocean.
他最著名的这次旅行是海中两个岛屿之间的约1000海里航程回归。

Far from drifting, as proposed by Sharp, Lewis found that ancient navigators would have known which course to steer by memorizing which stars rose and set in certain positions along the horizon, and this gave them fixed directions by which to steer their boats.
刘易斯发现，远非像夏普建议的那样漂流，古代航海家们会知道，通过背弃地平线上某些位置上的恒星，会引导哪条航道，从而给他们定下航向，引导他们的船。

paragraphs.brief: Edwin Doran的地理学家采取了完全不同的方法。
sentences: The geographer Edwin Doran followed a quite different approach.
Edwin Doran的地理学家采取了完全不同的方法。
He was interested in obtaining exact data on canoe sailing performance, and to that end employed the latest electronic instrumentation.
他有兴趣获得关于独木舟航行性能的确切数据，并为此采用了最新的电子仪器。

Doran traveled on board traditional sailing canoes in some of the most remote parts of the Pacific, all the while using his instruments to record canoe speeds in different wind strengths — from gales to calms — and the angle canoes could sail relative to the wind.
多兰在太平洋一些最偏远的地区乘坐传统的帆船，同时利用他的仪器记录从风向到平静的不同风力的独木舟速度，角独木舟与风相对可以航行。
In the process, he provided the first really precise attributes of traditional sailing canoes.
在此过程中，他提供了传统帆船的第一个真正准确的属性。

paragraphs.brief: Steven Horvath又提供了一份捐款。
sentences: A further contribution was made by Steven Horvath.
Steven Horvath又提供了一份捐款。
As a physiologist, Horvath’s interest was not in navigation techniques or in canoes, but in the physical capabilities of the men themselves.
作为一名生理学家，Horvath的兴趣不是航行技术或独木舟，而是人本身的体能。

By adapting standard physiological techniques, Horvath was able to calculate the energy expenditure required to paddle canoes of this sort at times when there was no wind to fill the sails, or when the wind was contrary.
通过调整标准生理技术，Horvath能够计算出在没有风来填满帆时或在风来反面时划划这种独木舟所需的能量支出。
He concluded that paddles, or perhaps long oars, could indeed have propelled for long distances what were primarily sailing vessels.
他的结论是，桨，或许是长桨，确实可以长途推进主要是帆船。

paragraphs.brief: 最后，由P.Wall Garrard领导的一个小组进行了重要的研究，在此案中，在安全地留在实验室时进行了调查。
sentences: Finally, a team led by P. Wall Garrard conducted important research, in this case by making investigations while remaining safely in the laboratory.
最后，由P.Wall Garrard领导的一个小组进行了重要的研究，在此案中，在安全地留在实验室时进行了调查。

Wall Garrard’s unusual method was to use the findings of linguists who had studied the languages of the Pacific islands, many of which are remarkably similar although the islands where they are spoken are sometimes thousands of kilometres apart.
沃尔·加拉尔的不寻常方法就是使用学习太平洋岛屿语言的语文学家的研究结果，其中许多语言非常相似，尽管他们所讲的岛屿有时相隔数千公里。
Clever adaptation of computer simulation techniques pioneered in other disciplines allowed him to produce convincing models suggesting the migrations were indeed systematic, but not simultaneous.
对其他学科的计算机模拟技术进行聪明的调整，使他能够提出令人信服的模型，表明迁移确实是系统性的，但不是同时进行的。

Wall Garrard proposed the migrations should be seen not as a single journey made by a massed fleet of canoes, but as a series of ever more ambitious voyages, each pushing further into the unknown ocean.
沃尔·加拉德建议，迁移不应被视为由大批独木舟组成的船队进行的单程，而应视为一系列更加雄心勃勃的航行，每个航行都进一步推进到未知的海洋。

paragraphs.brief: 我们从这项研究中了解到什么太平洋导航和漏洞？
sentences: What do we learn about Pacific navigation and voyaging from this research?
我们从这项研究中了解到什么太平洋导航和漏洞？
Quite correctly, none of the researchers tried to use their findings to prove one theory or another; experiments such as these cannot categorically confirm or negate a hypothesis.
十分正确的是，没有一个研究人员试图利用他们的调查结果来证明一种或另一种理论；这样的实验不能明确证实或否定一种假设。
The strength of this research lay in the range of methodologies employed.
这种研究的优势在于所采用的方法范围。

When we splice together these findings we can propose that traditional navigators used a variety of canoe types, sources of information and navigation techniques, and it was this adaptability which was their greatest accomplishment.
当我们把这些发现结合在一起时，我们可以建议传统导航员使用各种独木舟类型、信息来源和导航技术，而这种适应能力是他们的最大成就。
These navigators observed the conditions prevailing at sea at the time a voyage was made and altered their techniques accordingly.
这些航海人员观察了航行时海上的普遍状况，并相应改变了他们的技术。

Furthermore, the canoes of the navigators were not drifting helplessly at sea but were most likely part of a systematic migration; as such, the Pacific peoples were able to view the ocean as an avenue, not a barrier, to communication before any other race on Earth.
此外，航海者的独木舟并非无助地在海上漂流，而是最有可能是系统性移徙的一部分；因此，太平洋人民能够将海洋视为在地球上任何其他种族之前进行交流的一条途径，而不是障碍。
Finally, one unexpected but most welcome consequence of this research has been a renaissance in the practice of traditional voyaging.
最后，这一研究的一个出人意料但最受欢迎的结果是，传统窥探习俗的复兴。
In some groups of islands in the Pacific today, young people are resurrecting the skills of their ancestors, when a few decades ago it seemed they would be lost forever.
今天，在太平洋的一些岛屿上，青年人正在恢复其祖先的技能，而几十年前，他们似乎将永远失去这些技能。

items.en: The Pacific islands were uninhabited when migrants arrived by sea from Southeast Asia.
items.zh: 太平洋岛屿在移徙者从东南亚经海路抵达时无人居住。
items.why: 了明确写出“无人居住直到…从东南亚航来",与题干一致。

items.en: Andrew Sharp was the first person to write about the migrants to the islands.
items.zh: 安德鲁・夏普是第一个写到岛上的移民。
items.why: 20 世纪初就有人写过浪漫化的描述。Sharp 只是第一个“严肃评估”而非“第一个写" 的人。题干与原文矛盾。

items.en: Andrew Sharp believed migratory voyages were based more on luck than on skill.
items.zh: 安德鲁·夏普相信迁徙航行更多地是基于运气而不是技能
items.why: 原文写道“Sharp对 " 英雄观 " 提出质疑，声称航海者的专门知识有限，岛上的定居不是系统性的，因为漂流独木舟更依赖幸运”，支持题干所说的“安德鲁·夏普相信迁徙航行更多地是基于运气而不是技能”。

items.en: Despite being controversial, Andrew Sharp’s research had positive results.
items.zh: Andrew Sharp的研究虽然有争议但还是取得了积极的成果
items.why: 虽有争议，但它“激发了新的兴趣并促成有价值的研究”,即产生积极结果。

items.en: Edwin Doran disagreed with the findings of Lewis’s research.
items.zh: Edwin Doran不同意刘易斯的研究结果。
items.why: 多兰采用了与刘易斯不同的研究方法。方法不同不能推出他反对刘易斯的研究结果，文章也没有记载这种争论。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: David Lewis’s research was different because
items.zh: 大卫·刘易斯的研究不同，因为
correct: he observed traditional navigators at work
他观察了传统的导航员在工作

items.en: What did David Lewis’s research discover about traditional navigators?
items.zh: David Lewis的研究对传统航海家有何发现？
correct: They knew which direction they were sailing in
他们知道他们往哪个方向航行

items.en: What are we told about Edwin Doran’s research?
correct: Canoe characteristics were recorded using modern instruments
使用现代仪器记录了独木舟特性

items.en: Which of the following did Steven Horvath discover during his research?
items.zh: 史蒂文·霍瓦特在研究期间发现了以下哪些情况？
correct: Human energy may have been used to assist sailing canoes
人类的能量可能已经用来协助帆船航行

items.en: What is the writer’s opinion of Wall Garrard’s research?
items.zh: 作者对沃尔·加拉尔的研究有何看法？
correct: He is impressed by the originality of the techniques used
他对所使用的技术的独创性印象深刻

items.en: One limitation in the information produced by all of this research is that it
items.zh: 所有这些研究所产生的信息的一个限制是：
items.answer: C · was not conclusive evidence in support of a single theory
items.solution: 并不是支持单一理论的确凿证据

items.en: The best thing about this type of research
items.answer: A · was the variety of experimental techniques used

items.en: The most important achievement of traditional navigators
items.zh: 传统导航员最重要的成就
items.answer: D · was being able to change their practices when necessary
items.solution: 必要时能够改变其做法

items.en: The migration of people from Asia to the Pacific
items.zh: 从亚洲向太平洋迁移人口
items.answer: E · was the first time humans intentionally crossed an ocean
items.solution: 人类第一次故意穿越海洋

第 4 段 · 第 1 句
第 8 段 · 第 2 句

题干问“这种研究最好的东西”。定位句写到“这种研究的优势在于所采用的方法范围”。

人民如何迁移到太平洋岛屿
